qlStatus: **The QL thread closed cleanly.** He went into legs with the QL tight from Thursday's heavy figure-8s @50 — exactly the W18D4 caution — and flagged it himself ('ql definitely tight from all the figure eights, will take it easy'). He self-managed it: deliberately easy squat structure (70 intermediary, only 2 working sets at 80), lots of stretch breaks, and pigeon between Bulgarian sets. Result the next day (Saturday): 'feels fine; definitely sore QL but not even close to spasms.' So the heavy-figure-8-before-legs cost is real (tight QL the next day) but manageable — not a ban, just a 'take legs easy + mobility breaks' flag. The Smith Bulgarian at 45 cleared the QL for a 2nd straight week. W9 QL issue stays suppressed. (Calf raise not separately narrated — not asserting either way.)
lessonsForFutureWeeks: **Heavy figure-8 → tight-QL-before-legs is now empirically confirmed — but manageable, not a ban.** He went into legs with the QL tight from W18D4's figure-8 @50 (the exact caution), self-managed it (easy squats, stretch breaks, pigeon between sets), and it held — sore but no spasm. So: keep layering the heavy figure-8 if he wants, just expect QL tightness into Friday and take legs easy + add mobility breaks. If a future week needs legs fresh, keep the heavy (50) figure-8 off Thursday (light / around-the-world fine).

**Squat: he added a 70 intermediary ROM-builder and ran only 2 working sets at 80 — a deliberate ROM-first restructure.** Stated goal: fix ROM + the mid-range; hips still super tight; 'ROM more important than absolute weight right now.' ROM 'better than last week, ~85%.' W19 squat is a spotlight (depth refresh) — formalize the 45→70→80 ROM-building ramp and make depth the explicit lever. Hold 80; don't push load.

**Leg curl settled at 80 working (from 90), 'feels pretty correct vs what it used to be.'** Form-first: the 70 primer grooves the pattern, 80 executes correctly — better-quality work than grinding 90 with drift. Leg curl is the W19 spotlight: drill the correct feel at 80, let 90 return only once the pattern's grooved. Don't push back to 90 (not a regression — the correct feel is the win).

**Leg press was unusually brutal ('sweating like a wet dog, never happened').** User's read: pre-fatigued QL/core (from the figure-8s) + the deep-ROM core stimulus = the core is the exposed weak link, 'should do more to wake it up.' One session with a clear pre-fatigue confound — don't over-read it. But the instinct is worth a light W19 test: a short core/QL primer in the legs warmup, and watch whether the leg press normalizes when the QL ISN'T pre-fatigued. Frame as a question, not a load change.

**Pigeon between Bulgarian sets 'really helped' — keeper.** Self-found intra-set mobility (like the mini-dip warmup find on push). Add it to the Bulgarian station as an option: pigeon on the bench between sets keeps the hip/QL loose under the split-squat load. He also took lots of stretch breaks generally — good self-regulation on a QL-tight day.
